translationRepairs: When Yuwen Jiong rose in rebellion, Emperor Gaozu was deeply concerned and told Shikang, "Fen and Jiang were once the border between Zhou and Qi—this uprising may shake the region.
When Yuchi Jiong rose in rebellion, Emperor Gaozu was deeply concerned and told Shikang, "Fen and Jiang were once the border between Zhou and Qi—this uprising may shake the region.
尉迥 is Yuchi Jiong (尉遲迥), not Yuwen Jiong.
He was posthumously made grand general with the temple name Wen.
He was posthumously made grand general with the posthumous name Wen.
諡 is a posthumous name, not a temple name.

While still young under the Northern Wei he entered the inner guard, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han'an, married Princess Xiangle, daughter of Zhou Emperor Wen, and received the rank of Pillar of State, Third Rank.

While still young under the Northern Wei he entered the inner guard, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han'an, married Princess Xiangle, daughter of Zhou Emperor Wen, and received the rank of Equal in Ceremonial to the Three Excellencies.
儀同三司 means 'Equal in Ceremonial to the Three Excellencies', not 'Pillar of State, Third Rank'.
A year later he was recalled to court as grand master of the ministry of the people, promoted to upper pillar of state, and then transferred to grand master of the department of accounts.

A year later he was recalled to court as grand master of the ministry of the people, promoted to Supreme Commander Unequalled in Honor, and then transferred to grand master of the department of accounts.
上開府 (上開府儀同三司) is not 'pillar of state' (柱國).
When Gaozu was chancellor he followed his uncle Xiaokuan against Yuwen Jiong at Xiangzhou and, for his merit, was made pillar of state and Duke of Xiangyang with two thousand households.
When Gaozu was chancellor he followed his uncle Xiaokuan against Yuchi Jiong at Xiangzhou and, for his merit, was made pillar of state and Duke of Xiangyang with two thousand households.
尉迥 is Yuchi Jiong (尉遲迥), not Yuwen Jiong.
When Gaozu was chancellor, Yuwen Jiong plotted treason; the court had wind of it and sent Yi's uncle Xiaokuan posthaste to replace him.
When Gaozu was chancellor, Yuchi Jiong plotted treason; the court had wind of it and sent Yi's uncle Xiaokuan posthaste to replace him.
尉迥 is Yuchi Jiong (尉遲迥), not Yuwen Jiong.
He played a major part in defeating Yuwen Dun and pacifying Xiangzhou.
He played a major part in defeating Yuchi Dun and pacifying Xiangzhou.
尉惇 is Yuchi Dun (尉遲惇), not Yuwen Dun.
He was posthumously made upper pillar of state, granted ten thousand bolts of silk, with the temple name Jing.
He was posthumously made upper pillar of state, granted ten thousand bolts of silk, with the posthumous name Jing.
諡 is a posthumous name, not a temple name.
Under Zhou Emperor Wu he rose repeatedly through military merit to upper pillar of state and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu with eight hundred households.
Under Zhou Emperor Wu he rose repeatedly through military merit to Upper Equal in Ceremonial and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu with eight hundred households.
上儀同 is 'Upper Equal in Ceremonial', not 'upper pillar of state' (上柱國).
Eloquent as an envoy, he rose to lower imperial bearer grand master with the added rank of upper pillar of state.
Eloquent as an envoy, he rose to lower imperial bearer grand master with the added rank of Upper Equal in Ceremonial.
上儀同 is 'Upper Equal in Ceremonial', not 'upper pillar of state'.
Lady Xi of Gaoliang brought her forces to welcome him, and he pressed on into Lingnan.
Lady Xian of Gaoliang brought her forces to welcome him, and he pressed on into Lingnan.
洗氏 as a surname is read Xiǎn (Lady Xian of Gaoliang).
In Renshou, Gaozu betrothed Chong's daughter to Prince Yang Guang and made him minister of the people.
In Renshou, Gaozu took Chong's daughter as consort for Yang Jian, Prince of Yuzhang and made him minister of the people.
豫章王暕 is Yang Jian, Prince of Yuzhang, not Yang Guang.
When Gaozu was chancellor he made Shou pillar of state, third rank, then Duke of Hua with five thousand households for pacifying Jiong.
When Gaozu was chancellor he made Shou Equal in Ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, then Duke of Hua with five thousand households for pacifying Jiong.
儀同三司 is 'Equal in Ceremonial to the Three Excellencies'.
Under the Zhou he rose to upper pillar of state and prefect of Guang.
Under the Zhou he rose to Supreme Commander Unequalled in Honor and prefect of Guang.
上開府 is not 'upper pillar of state' (上柱國).
He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi, was made pillar of state, then grand master of the imperial clan.
He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi, was made Commander Unequalled in Honor, then grand master of the imperial clan.
開府 is not 'pillar of state' (柱國).
Shou's younger brother Ji rose to vice minister of imperial sacrifices and Marquis of Anyi.
Shou's younger brother Ji rose to vice minister of imperial sacrifices and Earl of Anyi.
安邑縣伯 is an earldom (伯), not a marquisate.
He was posthumously made grand general and prefect of Qing with the temple name Jian.
He was posthumously made grand general and prefect of Qing with the posthumous name Jian.
諡 is a posthumous name, not a temple name.
Marriage to an imperial princess brought him pillar of state with insignia of office and vice director of the secretariat.
Marriage to an imperial princess brought him Commander Unequalled in Honor, Equal in Ceremonial to the Three Excellencies and vice director of the secretariat.
開府儀同三司 is not 'pillar of state'.
When Wang Qian of Yi rebelled he served as campaign chief administrator under Liang Rui and was made pillar of state, third rank.
When Wang Qian of Yi rebelled he served as campaign chief administrator under Liang Rui and was made Equal in Ceremonial to the Three Excellencies.
儀同三司 is 'Equal in Ceremonial to the Three Excellencies'.
In Kaihuang year one he was made pillar of state, enfeoffed Baron of Xincheng, and given command of the setting pillar of cavalry.
In Kaihuang year one he was made Commander Unequalled in Honor, enfeoffed Baron of Xincheng, and made cavalry general in charge of furnishings.
開府 is not 'pillar of state'; 掌設驃騎 is a cavalry-general post.
He began under the Zhou as literary scholar to Prince Wen of Qi.
He began under the Zhou as literary attendant (文學) to the Prince of Qi.
文學 is the office; there is no 'Prince Wen' — the Prince of Qi is Yuwen Xian.
He was soon made acting left heir apparent of the crown prince and raised to earl.
He was soon made acting left mentor (左庶子) of the crown prince and raised to earl.
左庶子 is an official of the heir's household, not an heir.
The former emperor had Gao Feng and others present Prince Xiang to me as companion.
The former emperor had Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, Yuan Min and others present Wang Zixiang to me as companion.
高熲 is Gao Jiong; 王子相 is Wang Zixiang, not 'Prince Xiang'; the omitted names are restored.
Under Zhou Emperor Wu he was grand secretariat director, Duke of Wencheng, pillar of state, and dominated the court.
Under Zhou Emperor Wu he was grand secretariat director, Duke of Wencheng, Commander Unequalled in Honor, and dominated the court.
開府 is not 'pillar of state'.
When Gaozu took the throne Ang recovered, was made upper pillar of state, and appointed prefect of Lu.
When Gaozu took the throne Ang recovered, was made Supreme Commander Unequalled in Honor, and appointed prefect of Lu.
上開府 is not 'upper pillar of state' (上柱國).
Gaozu was delighted and appointed him grand director of the imperial clan.
Gaozu was delighted and appointed him Grand Minister of Rites (大宗伯).
大宗伯 heads the Ministry of Rites in the Zhou six-ministry system.
Ang's son Diao began as secretariat gentleman and became attending censor.
Ang's son Diao began as gentleman of the palace library and became attending censor.
秘書郎 is a palace-library post, not the secretariat.
